r2title.text: Round 2 · Wavebell's shape in Tide's style · deep blue and cyan

r2read.text:
How to read round 2

• Shape: Wavebell (two wave arcs, a core, five tentacles as a level meter).
• Tile: Tide's gradient tile, recoloured in deep blues and cyans.
• “Transparent lines”, three ways: translucent white (2, 5, 6, 8), glass tubes with a bright rim and a clear core (3, 4, 7), and an outlined core like Tide's bell (5).
• Translucent and glass lines fade at 16–32 px. The chosen variant gets hand-tuned small sizes with solid lines.
• My picks: 4 Deep Sea, then 2 Clearwater.

cmptitle.text: Now Playing · two styles · same placeholder track

cmpnote.text:
Compare

• A · Artwork: the cover, blurred and darkened for contrast, fills the screen; the scrubber thumb is the one liquid-glass accent. The most immersive; breaks Misty's MAT-02 and MAT-04.
• B · Misty: the field's aurora takes the cover's hue and the cover stays a framed object; plain Veil thumb. Calmer, and Misty-conformant.
• Same layout, tokens and contrast rules in both.
• Placeholder artwork, title and lyrics were made for this mock-up.
• In the app both ship behind Appearance → Style from Milestone 2.

title.text: Jellyfesh · app icon concepts · for approval

brief.text:
How to review

• Pick one concept, or two to combine.
• Each one is drawn in layers (background, foreground, monochrome), so it can become a macOS 26 layered icon, an Android adaptive and themed icon, a GNOME icon with a symbolic version, and a Windows icon.
• Small sizes are shown as drawn. The chosen concept gets hand-tuned 16 and 32 px versions.
• Colours come from the Misty OKLCH conversion, so the icon and the interface share one palette.

dropped.text:
Explored and dropped

• Flagnote (bell as a note head, tentacle as stem and flag) and J-Drift (bell falling into a J): both read as umbrellas at small sizes.
• Aurelia (moon jelly seen from above): the four gonad rings read as the ⌘ key, and the rotated version formed hooks. Neither is acceptable.

risk.text:
Brand check before we commit

“Jellyfesh” sits close to “Jellyfin”, a media server we will also support as a source, and Jellyfin's own mark is a purple-to-cyan jellyfish-like arch. These concepts avoid that palette and silhouette, but the name needs a trademark search.

r3title.text: Round 3 · Depth's tile with Midnight's lines

r3read.text:
Round 3

• A is exactly what you asked for: Depth's tile with Midnight's cyan-tinted translucent lines.
• B adds a soft shadow, C uses Depth's outlined core, D starts the tile at aqua so the lines read more clearly.
• 32 and 16 px use a simplified master: one arc, the core and three tentacles, at full opacity.
• My pick: B, or D if you want more contrast.

ctltitle.text: Controls · four styles · same Misty tokens

ctlnote.text:
Four control styles, one design language

• A · Glass capsules (after Apple): the calmest; glyph-only transport, a seek bar that thickens while dragging. Its filled previous/next glyphs break Misty's ICO-03 (filled glyphs mark only active states) unless we keep them outlined.
• B · Fluent (after Microsoft): the most familiar on Windows; quiet square buttons, a precise ringed thumb, times at both ends.
• C · Expressive (after Google): the most playful; a play button that changes shape, a wavy played track, tonal pills. Adapted to Misty: separate pills instead of joined segments, and shapes change only between radii on Misty's scale.
• D · Blend (my pick): A's grouping, B's thumb and times, C's wave at half strength, Misty's segmented control.
• In all four: Misty colours and glass grades, 44 pt targets (48 dp on Android), one accent-filled action per view, motion from Misty's tokens. Waves stop when paused, in reduced motion and in Still mode.
• Pick one, or mix parts: for example D with C's play button.

r4title.text: Round 4 · icon B in ten colour combinations

r4read.text:
Round 4

• Same construction as B; only the colours change.
• 8 Abyss and 9 Ice are meant as dark and light appearances: macOS 26 and Android can switch the icon with the system appearance, so one main colour plus these two covers every case.
• My picks: 1 Original B or 2 Navy Tide as the main icon, with 8 Abyss for dark mode.

wmread.text:
Wordmark

• 1–3 are drawn in the icon's own line style: round strokes, tentacle curls on the j, y and l's. They're unique to Jellyfesh and need no font licence.
• 4–6 use Inter Display (SIL Open Font License), converted to outlines, so they render identically everywhere.
• Inside the app, text stays in the system font (Misty TYP-01); the wordmark appears only as artwork: About screen, website, installers, splash.
• My pick: 2 Monoline with bell, with 4 Type as the plain alternative.

icontitle.text: App icon · Ice and Steel by default, all ten in Settings

iconread.text:
How the app icon setting works

• Automatic (default): Ice in light appearance, Steel in dark.
• macOS 26: built into the layered icon, so the Dock, Finder and Launchpad follow the system. macOS 14–15: the Dock icon switches while Jellyfesh runs; Finder keeps Ice.
• Windows: the taskbar icon switches at once; the app updates its Start and desktop shortcuts too.
• Android: launchers can't follow dark mode reliably, so Automatic means Ice; the other nine are manual choices (a short confirmation, because some launchers move the icon). Android 13+ themed icons use the monochrome layer.
• Linux: one icon (Ice) from the app's metadata; the picker is hidden.

brandtitle.text: Wordmark · formal capitals and a fancier home page

brandread.text:
Wordmark usage

• Formal (spaced capitals, one colour): About window, installers, documents, legal pages, press.
• Home page hero: pick one of A, B or C below.
• A · Bioluminescent: the monoline wordmark as glowing glass tubes in a dark sea.
• B · Tentacle flourish: the j, the l's and the y trail long tentacles; on the website they can sway slowly (off with reduced motion).
• C · Aurora glass capitals: the formal capitals in frosted glass over an aurora, tying the two together.
• My pick: A, or C if you want the home page to match the formal mark.
